criteria.expectation: Report identifies that SchemaV1.Hike.distance was renamed to SchemaV2.Hike.distanceKm but the V1->V2 stage is a plain lightweight migration with no originalName mapping and no custom stage copying values, so existing distances are dropped and distanceKm takes its default of 0.

Report cites file and line evidence from at least SchemaV2.swift (distanceKm declared without @Attribute(originalName:)) and HikeMigrationPlan.swift (MigrationStage.lightweight for v1ToV2, including the comment claiming it is enough).

Report notes that Tests/HikeMigrationTests.swift only uses an in-memory SchemaV2 store with freshly inserted data and never opens a V1-seeded store, so it cannot detect the value loss; this also explains why fresh installs and green tests hid the bug.

Report proposes a concrete change: either @Attribute(originalName: "distance") on the renamed property or a custom MigrationStage that copies old values, plus a test that seeds an on-disk V1 store, migrates, and asserts distanceKm equals the seeded value.

Report presents the cause as strongly indicated by the source but does not claim to have reproduced the data loss or observed the 0.0 km result at runtime; wording such as 'based on source' or 'would' is used where appropriate.

Report explicitly distinguishes source review from actions not performed (building, running tests, migrating a real or sample V1 store) and lists what remains unverified, e.g. actual SwiftData behavior on a real upgrade.
Report does not claim to have edited, created, or deleted any input file, and any fixes are presented as proposals only.

Report does not state as a confirmed defect that distance values are lost or reset in the V1->V2 migration; it acknowledges the custom stage copies legacyDistance into distanceKm and that the test seeds a V1 store and asserts the value.
Report states that nothing was built or run, so the migration and test passing at runtime (e.g. the custom stage with originalName and didMigrate behaving as intended) remains unverified.

Any extra suggestions (e.g. more test cases, removing legacyDistance in a later version, error handling) are explicitly labeled optional, low priority, or nice-to-have, and the report does not demand a rewrite of the migration.
Report cites file and line evidence for why the migration looks correct (e.g. HikeMigrationPlan.swift custom stage, SchemaV2.swift originalName attribute, test in HikeMigrationTests.swift).
Report does not claim to have edited, created, or deleted any input file; any suggestions are proposals only.
